Upheld in part (Q9, a guard for a case the code cannot reach). The try/catch around `slugify` and the `slug === ""` fallback can never fire: entry.ts:48-63 never throws and returns "entry" for an empty slug. The finding's second claim is wrong. `slugify` already handles a reserved slug (`RESERVED.test(slug) ? `${slug}-entry``), so `con` is not left unhandled. That part is dropped.

Lowered to advisory. The gap is real: `extraPools` (brief.ts:142-175) adds the linked projects' rows with no `receivedMarks` check, so a muted member's received memory in a linked project reaches the brief labelled `from <project>`. But the person who sees it is the same member who received it, and per ADR 0026 any member may read any item. Muting is a display preference, not an access boundary, so no broader audience gets personal data and the rubric's defect does not apply. It is a correctness gap against AC-75 ("a muted server or member hides it") for the tests and the criteria.

Upheld on the diff-line branch (Q1). The project list's `sharing` comes from `levelOf`, which returns the policy row's sending level. `effectiveLevel` (src/sharing/levels.ts:151) turns `receive` into `local`, so the dock can never show Receive only, which AC-24 requires. `chooseLevel` (ProjectsView.vue:139) returns early when `level === p.sharing`, so a project at Receive only cannot be set back to Nothing from the dock. No capture can show that dead control or the cause.

Upheld (Q1/Q3). `compareSnapshot` returns on every page with `more` true, then builds `seen` from the last page's items alone (inbound.ts:629-642; it is called once per page at :539). On a snapshot longer than one page, every `received` row from an earlier page is deleted with its file, and every `sent` row from an earlier page is cleared and re-sent on base 0. This goes against spec.md:180. Every restore, rejoin, 410 and instance change triggers it, nothing counts or reports it, and nothing undoes it.

Upheld (Q1). The pull loops are built once from `confirmedServers` at start (run.ts:330). A server confirmed while `sync --auto` runs is swept but never pulled, status shows it ok, and only doctor's 24-hour check would ever reveal it. That is a failure nobody would see in the first hour.

Upheld (Q1/Q4, a core-table write bypassing the core store's writer). A later revision of a received memory runs `UPDATE memories SET title = ?, body = ? …` from src/sync and never calls `refreshMemoryVector`. The base routes every change to a memory's text through src/store/memories.ts, whose insertMemory update path calls `refreshMemoryVector` (memories.ts:89), and the spec puts received-memory writes there (`deleteReceivedMemory`, memories.ts:184). The old text's vector stays, and `healVectors` only fills missing vectors. The follow-up `UPDATE memories SET status, created_at` at inbound.ts:265 is the same bypass.

Upheld (Q1/Q5, a data loss). `CARRIED` brings the live `sharing_ledger`, received rows included, into the copy but leaves out `sharing_received_memories` (backup.ts:134-143). A memory received after the backup comes back as a ledger row with no provenance, which `receivedMemoryRow` (ledger.ts:597-603) reads as deduped (`memoryId: null`). The next upsert with the same hash is skipped, so the memory never returns. The reverse also happens: a copy tombstoned since then comes back alive, and the cursor is already past its tombstone.

Upheld (Q5, erasure). `orphanServerIds` finds orphans only through `knowledge_received` (`receivedServerIds`, index-store.ts:1559) and folders under the received root, never through `sharing_received_memories`. A server dropped by a restore that delivered only memories, or whose folder is already gone, is never cleaned up. Its teammates' memories and names stay, against the erasure ADR 0027 D-6 promises and the restore's own `pendingDeletion` report.

Upheld (Q2/Q6). `deleteReceivedMemory` runs `UPDATE memories … WHERE superseded_by = ?`, and no index covers `memories.superseded_by` (core 0001_init.sql has none). `deleteServerReceived` and `reconcileReceived` call it once per received memory inside one `guarded` write transaction (received.ts:341-350), so a large server removal holds the write lock across N full scans of a growing table. The missing index is old debt; the new per-row scan under the lock is the change's.

Upheld (Q2, a new query scanning a growing table). `HELD_PIN`'s correlated NOT EXISTS filters `sharing_ledger` on direction, item_kind, local_hash and a leading-wildcard LIKE. The ledger's only key is (destination, item_kind, item_uid, direction), so it scans the ledger once per pinned entry on every session start. `withRevisions` (line 1080) scans the same way on every search.

Upheld (Q2). In `RECEIVED_VISIBLE`, `NOT EXISTS (… knowledge_entries e2 WHERE e2.id = x.id)` has no index on `knowledge_entries.id` (its key is (repo_id, id)), so each received row scans the entries. `searchReceived` joins on `x.fts_rowid` (line 1039), which migration 8 does not index (0008_knowledge_received.sql indexes only (project_id, server_id) and id). These are new reads over growing tables.

Upheld (Q1, data loss). In `applyPage`, any error other than a `locked` KnowledgeError is logged and counted `skipped` (inbound.ts:315-320), and the cursor is then saved past the page. That revision never lands until the item changes again. The ten-try set-aside covers only dirty/locked rows, and the snapshot repairs entries only, never memories.
